Under this rule, you may object to answering any questions from Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecutor, or even from the Judges, if you believe that your answer might incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and, as a consequence, you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question. But in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled under such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence, save and except the offence of giving false testimony. utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm now going to read a brief summary of Mr. Brdjanin's statement in English. [In English] Radoslav Brdjanin became a member of the SDS in 1990. Between May the 5th of 1992 and July the 17th, 1992, he was the President of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina (ARK) and later he became the minister for urban planning and construction in the Republika Srpska. He was also elected deputy in the Assembly of the Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska deputy prime minister for the economy. On 8th of March, 1995, he was relieved from all his duties in the government and party. The reason why the Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka (ZOBL), the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina (ZOBK) and the ARK were established was to gain greater economic independence from the authorities in Sarajevo. The ARK statute was written for all three nations and all municipalities in Krajina were invited to join the region of Krajina. In 1990 and 1991, more than other parts of BH, Krajina felt the tensions and proximity of the fighting in Croatia, where military facilities of the JNA came under attack and Serbian people were discriminated against. Moreover, the leadership of the SDA began promoting the independence of BH and their deputies publicly started speaking against Yugoslavia and the JNA. As a result, the original economic project to create a region of Krajina acquired a political dimension. There were men in the region of Krajina who were for the unification of the two Krajinas and proclamation of the Republic of Krajina, but the SDS was against this. In April 1992, Prime Minister Djeric sent instructions for the establishment of Crisis Staffs in municipalities, but not in the region. The ARK Crisis Staff was established as the co-ordinating body at the regional level and Mr. Brdjanin was nominated as its president. The ARK Crisis Staff was not supported by the central authorities in Pale. Krajina was cut off from the rest of the Serbian Republic of BH until 28th of June, 1992, when a corridor was opened. However, the consequences of being cut off continued because two or three months were necessary for the supply to Krajina to start meeting the minimum requirements. The break between Banja Luka and Pale was not complete but communication was rendered extremely difficult. Mr. Brdjanin did not receive any instruction from Pale or Dr. Karadzic about his work or the work of the ARK Crisis Staff while it existed. The ARK Assembly and Executive Committee existed at the same time as the ARK Crisis Staff. The ARK Crisis Staff did not have premises to hold its meetings, it did not employ anyone, and, in other words, was superfluous. As for the relations between the ARK Crisis Staff and the municipalities, there was no subordination and the municipalities independently decided whether they would or would not implement the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff. Nothing could be done to punish municipal organs if they failed to implement decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff. From the very beginning, the ARK Crisis Staff fought against all paramilitary formations, regardless of the ethnic composition, and all citizens who had unauthorised weapons had to return them and place themselves under the command of the legal armed forces of the Territorial Defence. The ARK Crisis Staff tried to include Muslim, Croats, and members of the other nations in the community; however, sensitive information was being leaked. The Serbian soldiers were frustrated because they witnessed deaths and wounding of their loved ones by members of the same nation who held top positions in the Serbian state and who might have, at the same time, been leaking information to the enemy. As a result, the ARK Crisis Staff decided on 22nd of June, 1992, to appoint Serbs who unconditionally accepted the newly formed state structures, who respected the state institutions, laws, and regulations, to sensitive top positions from where information could be leaked. The guiding principle was that top positions could not be held by persons who rejected the state organs of the Serbian Republic of BH. President Karadzic used his authority granted by the constitution to appoint Muslims and Croats as judges and prosecutors alongside with Serbs. However, when the Republika Srpska Assembly convened on 12th of August, 1992, the deputies agreed not to re-elect Muslims and Croatians as a temporary measure during war time, despite Dr. Karadzic's pressure for his decisions to be ratified. The position of the ARK Crisis Staff about Muslims and Croats leaving the ARK never included forcible transfer or deportation. Individuals who decided to leave the ARK were required to have a certificate of departure which listed their belongings, as a proof that a person was voluntarily leaving and in order to allow the ARK Crisis Staff in order to protect the rights of these persons with regard to their property. Although against any form of forcible relocation of the people, the ARK Crisis Staff believed in enabling the reciprocal exchange of those civilians who expressed their wish to leave. On 10th of June, 1992, the ARK Crisis Staff adopted a decision that only women, children, and the elderly could leave the ARK voluntarily and that their departure should be effected in co-operation with the humanitarian societies. If able-bodied non-Serbs voluntarily decided to leave, the police first wanted to check whether they had been involved in combat operations against the Serbian armed forces or committed a crime. On 12th of June, 1992, the ARK Crisis Staff adopted a decision to establish an agency which would regulate the needs of the civilians who wanted to leave and exchange of their houses with Serbs. The work of the agency focused on providing assistance for the departure of all three ethnic communities. In June 1992, there were several thousand refugees in Banja Luka of Serbian ethnicity who entered abandoned flats and houses without authorisation. In order to stop this, the ARK Crisis Staff adopted a decision for all abandoned properties, regardless of who owned it, to be declared state property until the return of the original owner. In addition, Mr. Brdjanin urged the confiscation of property of the deserters from the VRS and all war profiteers. The opinion of President Karadzic on housing was that according to international law and standards, the housing policy in times of war should be temporary, the property of everyone should be respected, and he favoured compensation to all Muslims who left RS and could not return. President Karadzic has always promoted respect for the Geneva Conventions and insisted on humane treatment of non-Serbian civilians and prisoners of war. In Assembly sessions, he always underlined the importance of respecting the international law of war. [Interpretation] This was the brief summary. There is only one document that I would first like to ask Mr. Brdjanin about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 23(g) of your statement, page 10 in Serbian you explain the reasons and the nature of the agency for relocation that had been established. Did you have the same opinion at the time as regards the reasons underlying this decision and the persons that it pertained to?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I have page 9, sub-item (g).

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes, what I said here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 1D5587.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Dragan Stegic is?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. 5587 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, we are still waiting for it to show up. 1D55817.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not 55187?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it is 55187.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Mr. Stegic, who is he, and was this news broadcast and when? And the date here is the 23rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's first find out what this document is about from the witness. Mr. Brdjanin, can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I can see, it has to do with the following. Mr. Stegic is a journalist, as far as I can remember. It's not only that I can remember, that's the way it was. He talked to Bojinovic. I cannot say whether it was broadcast or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Brdjanin, before going into the content of this document, what this document at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that it is being recounted here -- I mean why the agency was established and what its objective was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote it, in what context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the last paragraph to yourself or you can read it out loud if you wish.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: This was an interview between our reporter, Dragan Stegic, and Milos Bojinovic, president of the agency for aid in the resettlement of people and exchange of material goods in Banja Luka, Stegic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where Stegic worked? Was he employed by the electronic media or the printed media?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, Radio Banja Luka or a newspaper, I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this be a transcript of that interview?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I assume that that could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have an ERN number, probably the Prosecution knows how they obtained this document, but I'd like to tender it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was an unilluminating colloquy on this document. I don't -- the document was, as I understand it, seized by the OTP in February of 1998. That's all the information I have on it, so I'm not in a position to add a great deal at this point to our understanding of the provenance of the document. And, as I say, I don't think we heard much from the witness that enlightened us about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will mark it for identification until it is satisfied with its provenance.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D4055, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 405? There must be some kind of mistake here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D4055.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. At this point in time I have no further questions for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, as you somewhere noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in most part in writing, that is, your written witness statement, in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you will be cross-examined by the office -- by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, it's not referenced in your statement, but you are, of course, the same Radoslav Brdjanin who was tried here in this institution on charges related to your role in joint efforts to create a Serbian entity from which most non-Serbs would be permanently removed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, that is true that I was tried for that, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that trial was not a brief affair. It began in January of 2002 and ended on April 22nd, 2004; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Over 150 witnesses were heard live, that is, viva voce; over a hundred witnesses were heard through the submission in written statements. That's correct; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, I assume that that is the case. I'm sorry, but I'm not aware of the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And thousands of exhibits were produced and considered by the Trial Chamber; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at the end of that process, you were convicted of crimes committed against non-Serbs in 13 ARK municipalities, including Bosanski Novi, Kljuc, Prijedor, Sanski Most, and Banja Luka, Bosanska Krupa, and others; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I don't know how many municipalities, but I was sentenced to 30 years in prison finally.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can barely hear the witness. Could he please be asked to approach the microphone and could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, you are requested by the interpreters to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. I take it you don't dispute either the number of municipalities which were encompassed by your conviction or the specific municipalities that I recited? That is contained in the judgement.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, I'm not disputing the fact that the Prosecutor issued an indictment regarding all the municipalities that are listed there, but the question is what out of all of that is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you were convicted of persecutions, including deportation and forcible transfer; wilful killings; torture; wanton destruction of cities, towns, and villages; and destruction of religious institutions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: You perhaps know my judgement better than I do. It is true that I was convicted; however, in view of the newly created standards, especially over the past two years, I really do not know why it is that I've been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn to some of the things you say to this court in your statement that has now been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, one second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 20 of your statement indicates that there was no relationship of superiority or inferiority, no subordination or hierarchy between the ARK Crisis Staff and the municipal Crisis Staffs. Now, Mr. Brdjanin, that same position was part of your defence in the course of your long trial here, between 2002 and 2004; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the Trial Chamber, after hearing all that evidence, found that the ARK municipalities, with the exception of Prijedor, "unquestionably accepted the authority of the ARK Crisis Staff as an intermediate level of authority between the republic level and the municipalities to issue binding instructions." And that's -- those findings can be found at paragraph 200 and 205 of your judgement. Is that right? You recall that's essentially what the Trial Chamber found? I see you have the judgement. I'm just putting this on the record so it's clear, and you're looking at it now. So if you turn to paragraph 200 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, I think that Mr. Brdjanin has the appeals judgement in front of him, so perhaps that might create some confusion. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think you heard your counsel, sir. I'm referring to the trial judgement, not the appeals judgement. The trial judgement is the one that made these findings of fact; the appeals judgement affirmed those.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: May I take a look at that? I mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I -- do you read English, sir? Because I only have a copy --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that. Yes, give it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I think we have in e-court --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, so you know, we're trying to get that available to be seen electronically. I think that's happening as we speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't understand the problem, Mr. President. We're taking it from every possible angle. If you want to take a quick break, we'll have both the hard copy and the uploaded within just a -- within a few minutes. Maybe that's the simplest way to do it. I don't understand the -- unless -- I see it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it only in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As far as I know -- that's all I see at the moment. But in any event, I would be reciting the particular portion. utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I had turned your attention to paragraph 200 and paragraph 205. 200, as we see, states: "The ARK Crisis Staff, assuming all powers and functions of the ARK Assembly, acted as an intermediate level of authority between the Serbian BiH and the municipalities." And if we turn to paragraph --

utterances.text: Where is it in 200?

utterances.text: First sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we turn to 205 we see: "With the exception," again the first sentence, "of Prijedor municipality, all ARK municipalities unquestionably accepted the authority of the ARK Crisis Staff to issue instructions that were binding upon them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note those two sentences are without footnotes. I take it are they the findings? Are they referring to specific evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: These are the overall findings that encompass the broader factual -- specific factual findings that underpin them later in the judgement. I note -- I note in particular that this judgement, as others, related to witnesses who have been -- testified as we have discussed in court before are available to the Court. So I don't think Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic have any problem if the Court pursues the relationship between the broader findings and the underlying factual basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So I'm going to -- although I'll be referring to other portions of the judgement, Mr. Brdjanin, that relate to paragraph 20, I wanted to confirm, first of all, that the same position you took in paragraph 20 was taken in your trial and this was the conclusion of the Court?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to Prijedor, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, paragraph 20 of his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of his current statement before the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- which relates to the alleged ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Brdjanin, if it's at all helpful, I have a hard copy of the trial judgement in Serbian if you'd like to have that available.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 208, the Trial Chamber also noted that Prijedor was an exception in the sense that there was at some stage a dispute with the ARK authorities that arose from the position of the Prijedor authorities, that they were underrepresented on the ARK Crisis Staff. But nevertheless, Prijedor implemented the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff. That's what your Trial Chamber also found in connection with that particular ARK municipality; right? That's paragraph 208.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I don't know whether you're asking me to confirm now what is written in paragraph 208 or to say whether that had actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually asking you to confirm that that was the finding of the Trial Chamber. You're right, I understand that you took a contrary position at trial; that's precisely why I'm pointing out what the Trial Chamber found.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, that's why I didn't even need this judgement. I know that you're reading from the judgement and, yes, that is what was found by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And so you understand, Mr. Brdjanin, none of this was mentioned in the statement so I'm trying to put it in the record so this Trial Chamber has an accurate understanding of the background. Finally, with respect to the positions you took at trial and with respect to paragraph 20 here, the Trial Chamber found that the Defence submission that municipalities such as Prijedor, Sanski Most, Kljuc were "renegade municipalities," who acted independently of both the ARK Crisis Staff and the RS republic-level authorities was not true. That is, the Trial Chamber was satisfied "beyond a reasonable doubt" that the crimes charged were the implementation of a plan that originated "from the top level of the Bosnian Serb leadership and whose implementation by the municipalities was co-ordinated by the regional authorities of the ARK." And that's found at paragraph 209, and that accurately states the or reflects the position taken by the Defence in your trial and the findings of the Trial Chamber; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: It is well-known what the position of the Trial Chamber was since I was sentenced to 30 years in prison, but I don't know whether I have an opportunity now to say what I think about what is stated here in the judgement. This is the first time that I speak. I was not allowed to speak at all during the appeal or before that, and obviously my Defence did not manage to prove why the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region was simply a co-ordinating body or simply a service for the Crisis Staffs of the municipalities. By no way -- by no means was it superior to them or could it have imposed any kind of sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, at this point, Mr. Brdjanin, I think we understand that's your position, both by virtue of the fact, as we've just discussed, that it was your position during the trial and it's your position as reflected essentially in paragraph 20 and other parts of your statement. But let me turn to some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did Mr. Brdjanin testify in his case or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I don't believe so. But he can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't testify in your case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I sat there for two or three years like Ikebana, I don't know how to put it. I was not allowed to say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it was your decision not to testify in your case, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, testimony. But I'm talking about the trial in general, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me talk about a few specifics before I move on. For example, Mr. Brdjanin, municipality Crisis Staff presidents attended ARK Crisis Staff meetings, both to find out what was happening in the field within the ARK and elsewhere and to find out what they were supposed to do about it. So they came to get information about what was happening and to find out what they were to do next; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I have to answer by explaining why the presidents of the Crisis Staffs attended. It was at their proposal that the autonomous region staff was founded and they just came there for an exchange of information. As for the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region, they just kept minutes and checked, conditionally speaking, with regard to their agreements who had implemented what. So co-ordinating body would really be the best expression. However, what is even more important is you have three of my signatures at -- on 21 records of these meetings. That is what I attended. I saw on time that this was an exercise in futility --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, excuse me. Mr. Brdjanin, excuse me. Mr. Brdjanin, sorry, I make a quick -- few quick ground rules. First of all, I think we can see now that you're repeating precisely what's in your statement, and you're doing so not to answer my question but to argue about what you see is the implications of that answer. So you've had a chance --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry, sorry, sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So if -- please listen to what the question is and respond to that. We now have your statement before us. Okay. So if I understand it, you agree that on a routine basis, indeed, every Monday, you would meet with the municipality presidents and inform them about the political situation in the area?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did meet on Mondays whenever they met, but not with me because I said that I did not attend half of the meetings or perhaps even two-thirds of the meetings. So the meetings were held on Mondays and they did exchange information at these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 40458, please. That's a video-clip. I'd like to play that. Sorry, it's 40458A. That may help. And for the interpreters that's at English and B/C/S page 2, that would be the portion of the video where we'll hear speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not need to switch to Sanction?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. Brdjanin, tell us, why did you come and how do you see the latest developments in the Kotor Varos municipality? "Mr. Brdjanin, tell us, why did you come and how do you see the latest developments in the Kotor Varos municipality? "Let me tell you, my duty as the president of the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region is to visit all fronts. I must admit that most of the time I was in the corridor leading to Serbia, but simply my visit -- the reason for my coming here is that every Monday I must inform the presidents of all Crisis Staffs about the political situation in this area. We must clean up our area which unquestionably includes Kotor Varos and Jajce, and the most important battle which is underway and which I attended yesterday is the break-through to Serbia. Simply, we can see for ourselves that there can be no more negotiations with those waging war against us. Those who took up arms must be defeated, hand them over and total Serb authority must rule here."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that is a depiction of you at the time, Mr. Brdjanin, and that reflects your contemporaneous position about the meetings, the regular meetings, with presidents of municipalities -- presidents of Crisis Staffs, to advise them about the political situation in the area?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 40458A, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6512, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, this Trial Chamber has received evidence from municipalities concerning Crisis Staff meetings in municipalities and specifically concerning references to Crisis Staff members attending -- municipal Crisis Staff members attending ARK Crisis Staff meetings. I'm happy to show you the individual documents if you wish, but let me indicate what they reflect. P2606, which is the Crisis Staff book of minutes from Kljuc, indicates on 1 June 1992 - that's page 8 of the English and page 29 of the Serbian - that Veljko Kondic and Rajko Kalabic were sent to attend the Krajina Crisis Staff session. And June 1st is, indeed, a Monday, which I think can be judicially noticed. Same book of minutes reflects, at English page 14 through 16 and B/C/S pages 43 through 47, that on June 9th, 1992, a Tuesday, there was a report from the session of the Banja Luka regional Crisis Staff and Kondic informed the Kljuc Crisis Staff of the conclusions of the regional Crisis Staff session and remarked on the most important issues. And similarly, at English pages 16 through 19 and at B/C/S 49 through 61, on the 16th of June, 1992, another Tuesday, that is, the day after the Mondays that are referred to in your videotaped interview, Banjac, the president of the Crisis Staff reported to the Crisis Staff on the conclusion of the Banja Luka Crisis Staff on specific issues. And similarly, if we turn to 65 ter 07215, pages 1 in both the English and B/C/S, these are the minutes of the 29th Session of the Petrovac Crisis Staff held on the 9th of June, 1992, as mentioned, a Tuesday. And the first item is Rajko Novakovic, the president of the Crisis Staff, briefed those present on the conclusions adopted by the Autonomous Region Krajina Crisis Staff in Banja Luka. Now, all those references that we just saw, Mr. Brdjanin, reflect that indeed regular meetings were held at which presidents of Crisis Staffs or representatives of municipal Crisis Staffs would come to be briefed by you; correct? Or other members of the ARK Crisis Staff. I saw you nodding, sir, but you have to answer audibly for the record.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: When you showed the video-clip, I said that it was correct that I said that and that everything was arranged like that. However, it did not happen like that for many reasons. First of all, those were conditions of war. People could not attend regularly on Mondays, and I also stated other reasons because of which I did not attend when I saw that not everything was implemented. It's true that the report about Kljuc deals with how they would implement it; however, I know, though nobody may believe me, they implemented what suited them in their area if they had some material gain. If it didn't suit them, they didn't do it, and there were no sanctions against it. So it wouldn't turn out that I lied when I said that it wasn't held every Monday. I said for my statement that it was correct, the intention was such, but it could not be really implemented in practice, but it's true and it's correct that that was the intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could tender --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the witness to talk a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, did you say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was going to tender 65 ter 07215.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President, because this is a municipality not -- where no crimes are charged in the indictment. I don't think it's relevant that members of that municipality were reporting to the ARK; and therefore, we object.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The issue at the moment is not how many crimes occurred in how many places. The issue at this moment is the nature of the functioning of the ARK Crisis Staff and its relationship to the municipalities and it's obviously relevant for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, once the door is opened to this kind of evidence, then certainly we should be able to show that there were people who were affiliated with the ARK or attending ARK meetings who weren't involved in any crimes. And I think that will create a wider scope of the trial than the Chamber has so far wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not sufficient to have what we have in our transcript? The crux of the document was put to the witness. We heard the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not agreeing in its entirety, but agreeing in general about the need to -- need for a meeting and the meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view it does not need it, so shall we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Brdjanin, in fact the conclusions, decisions, of the ARK Crisis Staff, contrary to what you state in paragraph 20 and the position you took at your own trial, were considered by the municipality Crisis Staffs to be binding on them, as given to them by this intermediate level of authority, the ARK Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn to a few examples of that, if I may. P3497, English page 1 and B/C/S page 2. This is an announcement of the Kljuc Crisis Staff on the 8th of May, 1992, which states in part: "All decisions shall be made and tasks performed in compliance with the regulations and decisions of the organs of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina and the Serbian Republic of BiH ..." It's right in the middle of the page. So here we see Kljuc Crisis Staff expressly and publicly taking the position that the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff will be considered something that the Kljuc Crisis Staff will and should comply with; right? That was their public position, contemporaneously, that is, at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: You have this correct document. It's their document, I confirm that it is, but there is also the decision of the Una Sana region where Kljuc belongs, which are against this decision of the Crisis Staff of the ARK. The dates were the 12th and 14th of June, they met in Korcanica, and there are the documents which we provided during my trial. The municipalities were Kljuc, Bosanski Novi, Bosanski Petrovac, Serbian Bihac, Krupa on Una, Sanski Most, and Prijedor. That's the Sana-Una region. They met. As Mr. Ackerman called them, the renegade municipalities. I wouldn't call them renegade, but those who didn't -- Banja Luka never accepted the Crisis Staff and it's correct that there were municipalities that accepted it, but it depended on the decisions made by me and the other officials. I could do something in Celinac because I was the president of the Executive Board in Celinac, but there was no way to impose any sanctions against them in case they didn't obey us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I was going to look at a couple more municipalities, but let me, in the interests of time, simply focus for a moment on Prijedor, which was earlier discussed, and on various periods of time in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's first look at P3530, pages 1 in both languages, that's the -- a meeting on the 9th of May, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please, while we are waiting for the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 2 it's wrongly represented what the witness said. He didn't say that "it depended on my decisions which I made," but "it depended on my personal relations with the people in municipalities."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you agree with it, Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I said: On my personal relations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. We now have that document before us, and as we can see at -- on page 1, Mr. Kovacevic, the head of the Executive Committee, assures the assembled representatives that the functioning of the government at the level of Krajina can now be felt. And in addition, he states that: "Instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top ..." And on page 2 we can also see the president of the municipality, Mr. Stakic, emphasising that the constitution of the Serbian republic has been implemented since 30 April 1992. All right. So this is an early expression of the Prijedor authorities -- about the hierarchical structure between the republic level down through the ARK authorities to the municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: This is -- look at the date, the 9th of May, four days after the establishment of the Crisis Staff. And of course, in the beginning it was always idyllic. We can see that in ordinary life, as in a marriage, and then later on everything gets more and more watered down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn to two more decisions or two more documents from May, that's first P3536, English and B/C/S pages 3. And there we see the Prijedor Crisis Staff stating that the decisions of the responsible organs of the ARK are explicitly accepted to be one of the foundations for the work of the Prijedor Crisis Staff. Correct? And similarly, if I could turn to two days later, 22 May, that's P3708.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: No, no, no. Would you -- please, if you can bring back the document so we can look at the heading, the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: By all means. That was 3536.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Please, allow me just for a minute. The greatest confusion in my trial was the result of those headings. The Autonomous Region of Krajina existed. Its executive board or committee called the government and it says here on the basis of the decisions. It has nothing to do with the Crisis Staff. They operated all along and now they once referred to the autonomous region, once to the Crisis Staff, that caused the greatest confusion. I don't blame anyone, but I just wish to clarify that, if possible, in these sentences, one or two sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's apparently the same position as you just told us you took at trial. Maybe we can turn to page -- to P37 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Article number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Article 11, Mr. President, and 12 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. If you have done the reading, we'll move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that's P --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's P3708.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Brdjanin, in your previous answer you tried to focus on the broad encompassing language of Articles 11 and 12, referring to the ARK authorities, but if we look here at P3708, which is a meeting of 22 May, two days later, of the Prijedor Crisis Staff, it provides that -- or it directs all commercial and social enterprises to introduce permanent operational duty "in accordance with the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina ..." No ambiguity there, Mr. Brdjanin, is there? And that's a reflection of Prijedor's contemporaneous hierarchical organ -- hierarchical understanding; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: On the 26th of April, 1992, I'm talking this precisely, the Ministry of Defence called up mobilisation, where work obligation is understood as part of the mobilisation. In the Crisis Staff and all other organs were only those who were to execute this, to implement it, and here the idea is to imply that the author of the document was the Crisis Staff. No. We received the order and I too was assigned for work obligation. Some were assigned to armed forces, others had the work obligation in various ways, and there was Territorial Defence also. So it wasn't an original document of the Crisis Staff, as implied, but only implementation of what the ministry ordered on the 26th of April, 1992, to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's fast-forward to late June 1992 because you refer to this initial honeymoon period. So let's look at some period later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to P2740. That's a 22 June 1992 ARK Crisis Staff decision which is being forwarded by the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- Prijedor Crisis Staff. If we could turn to the -- let's just take a look at that underlying decision first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This refers to --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- prohibitions on various kinds of employment and --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: No, this is -- may I?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 3, please. And B/C/S page 4 for the benefit of the witness. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We can see the very next day the Prijedor Crisis Staff forwarding the ARK Crisis Staff decision for implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then if we could turn quickly to a related document, P2637. Page 1 refers to the earlier Crisis Staff document dated the 23rd of June, 1992; that's 02-111-236/92. And on page -- so that's what we looked at earlier, that was page 3 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S of the previous document. And finally let's turn to P2637, we can see the final report on its implementation. And that's at page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And there we see a report on the ARK Crisis Staff decision we looked at first of 22 June, that's 03-531 of 22 June 1992. And the document states that it "has been implemented in this public security station ..." So these documents that we've just looked at reflect in Prijedor, Mr. Brdjanin, the active implementation of ARK Crisis Staff decisions following the initial declaration that ARK Crisis Staff decisions would indeed be binding and the decisions were now being forwarded from the top through to the ARK Crisis Staff and to the municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Can you please bring back the original of the document dated the 22nd so that I may give an answer on the basis of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just looking at this document, just note the number is 03-531 of 22 June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then the witness has asked to see again P2740, at page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, that brings up something that I was also concerned about. I think that this practice of putting multiple documents to the witness and asking a question at the end is -- makes it very difficult for the witness. I notice on line 20 he tried to intervene and now he's asked to go back to another document. So I would ask that the Chamber order Mr. Tieger to elicit a comment from the witness after showing him an individual document, even if it's only to ask is this an example of whatever Mr. Tieger is trying to establish. But if we try to make the witness keep in his head three documents, I don't think it's fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, three documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Thank you. Let's see how it evolves, but putting so many documents before you ask a question, it may make witness difficult in answering the questions. Shall we continue? Let's have a break after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 2740 will be in front of you in just a moment, sir. That's the ARK Crisis Staff decision of 22 June.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I wanted to see this document again because you can see this is a document of general nature that I did sign, one of the few that I did sign. Later on I received documents that even mention prisoners. Here I have a judgement in my hand where the Chamber decided that I didn't have any powers over either the army or the police, especially it was very clear who dealt with the prisoners. I can confirm what this document said, but I cannot confirm what Simo Drljaca as chief of police said. When you look at the judgement and you see that the command in the police went along the chain of command within the Ministry of the Interior and this is a final judgement. That was the reason why I wanted to see this document again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said twice in line 18, 16 or 17, he said that this is a general document, whereas this has not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which document of general nature?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one that we see on the screen and that has been commented by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- heard that and it will be corrected in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's right in line 14. I don't know what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes, "you can see this is a document of general nature," yes, it's there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it was repeated later on several times and not recorded as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we take a break or would you like to wrap-up this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, that's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, just before the recess, at transcript page 34, you said: "Here I have a judgement in my hand where the Chamber decided that I didn't have any power over either the army or the police, especially it was very clear who dealt with the prisoners." In fact, that's not accurate. What your Trial Chamber, in fact, found with respect to your authority over the police can be found both at paragraphs 212, 213, and 214. So if we turn to 212, while it is true that the Chamber -- that your Trial Chamber found "the ARK Crisis Staff did not possess de jure power to issue orders to the police" - that's the last sentence of that short paragraph, 212 - it found, as we see reflected in paragraph 213, that: "In practice, however, the authorities of the ARK in general and the ARK Crisis Staff in particular had de facto authority over the police and co-ordinated the actions taken by the police." And it goes on to explain that in particular, orders to the police were issued and implemented concerning dismissals of non-Serbs from employment, disarmament of paramilitary units and individuals who illegally possessed weapons, selectively enforced against non-Serbs, and resettlement of the non-Serb population. That is a more accurate account of what your Trial Chamber found with respect to your authority over the police, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber -- I'm a bit confused because I'm trying to locate the conclusion that specifically refers to the armed forces and the police. Everything is accurate. The judgement was based on the de facto basis and based on the indicia. If people had de jure, they were found not guilty for de facto, but not in my case. But I'm not going to go into all these details, we don't want to listen to that. Anyway, I know that it is said here that the command responsibility was based on the superiority and subordination principle in the Ministry of the Interior. You used the word "order." I suppose that was used inadvertently because the Crisis Staff only delivered decisions. I never signed any document that contains the word "order."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Decisions which we have seen were considered binding by the municipal authorities, although I appreciate that you continued to dispute that point; correct? But that's what your Trial Chamber found, the municipal authorities did consider them binding?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Trial Chamber's conclusion. Perhaps my Defence failed to explain it correctly, but I stand by it and I assert that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as long as we have the trial judgement open, perhaps I can quickly turn to an issue raised in paragraph 23 of your statement, that is, that the position of the ARK --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, 23 is the paragraph at issue in your statement, where you state that the position of the ARK Crisis Staff about Muslims and Croats leaving the ARK never included forcible transfer or deportation.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Trial Chamber found - and the judgement reflected at paragraph 248 -- so it's paragraph 248 of the trial judgement, sir, which I'm turning to now - that another measure taken in furtherance of the strategic plan --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That paragraph reflected the Trial Chamber's finding that: "Another measure taken in furtherance of the Strategic Plan was the resettlement of the non-Serb population. This entailed the permanent expulsion of non-Serb inhabitants from the ARK and the repopulation of the area with Bosnian Serb refugees coming from other parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia."

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 248 is not identical with this. I'm not saying that it's incorrect, but there is some discrepancy, perhaps due to the English version. Is this my judgement at all? Well, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I can assure you I'm --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: No, no. I believe that, but what I have here is something completely different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you reading trial judgement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- oh, God. [In English] Sorry. [Interpretation] 248, yes. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And it continued that: "The resettlement policy within the territory of the Bosnian Krajina was co-ordinated at the regional level by the ARK Crisis Staff." And that the decisions -- "the ARK Crisis Staff decisions on the resettlement of non-Serbs are indicative of its involvement in the furtherance of the Strategic Plan ..." So with respect to the ARK's -- the ARK Crisis Staff's position on transfer -- forcible transfer/deportation, that was the finding of your Trial Chamber; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: During the main trial, I said to my Defence lawyer the following: There was no strategic plan ever about forcible relocation, particularly not in the sense as stipulated here. This is very serious. You can attribute everything to Serbs, but you can never attribute it to them having made some kind of plans because we are a people prone to improvisation. Quite simply, there was no plan. We followed the situation which dictated for people to be relocated rather than to be killed or to perish. This happened due to a variety of reasons, fear and everything else, not only on the Serbian part. People moved for various reasons. I'm not trying to justify this, I'm not commending this; I'm just telling you that that was what the situation required.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And one more paragraph, at 233, with respect to this same issue, the Trial Chamber found dismissals of non-Serbs was one of the first measures toward the implementation of the strategic plan referred to in the previous paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I'm very glad that you raised this issue because there were no dismissals as such but people were reassigned to different work-places, which was done by any political party anywhere in the world once they win elections. This is the practice in every country all over the world. This is not about dismissals. This is about not their being able to be in executive positions after the winning of the SDS, and specifically in view of the situation that prevailed that might have caused a rift among our ranks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak more slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, you're being asked by the interpreters to slow down your rate of speech. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second -- yes, Mr. Karadzic first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that it might be prejudicial to our defence, that's page 39, lines 24 and 25. This is nonsense what has been recorded. What he said was that it could damage our defence effort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A minute ago, Mr. Brdjanin, you said the following, I'll quote: "You can attribute everything to Serbs, but you can never attribute it to them having made some kind of plans because we are a people prone to improvisation." Do you remember having said that, Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you expand what kind of plans were you talking about as a result of improvisation? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can explain this very briefly. Due to the fact that we are a people of great individuals, and if we had only one party, we would have become an opposition to our own party. This is neither positive nor negative in my view. Believe me, at the state level and at the level of state plans, there were plans on how to defend ourselves or how to wrap-up our territories if others didn't want to live to us; however, there was never any plan or there were no political instructions how to harm other people, how to expel them, or how to disenfranchise them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I can understand that. But you talked about plan as a means of improvisation, so could you expand on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Since I'm an engineer by profession, you cannot have an improvised plan. What I actually wanted to say was that there were no such plans that are being mentioned in all the judgements, not only that against me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave it at that. Please continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, just to clarify, the answer you provided to my question about the paragraph regarding dismissals is -- that is -- sorry -- that is, people were reassigned to different work-places, it's the practice in every country around the world, et cetera, was the same position that was argued to -- by the Defence in your case to the Trial Chamber, but the paragraph I read to you at 233 about what the Trial Chamber found regarding dismissals, that is, that it was one of the first measures toward the implementation of the strategic plan, was in fact what your Trial Chamber did find; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: That is correct. The Trial Chamber reached conclusions which were totally contrary to what our assertions were, but that was completely beyond my control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to another topic, and that is some of your own efforts to implement the positions taken by the republic-level authorities. It's correct to say, is it not, that, for example, in 1991 you were actively involved in ensuring the implementation of policies formulated by Mr. Karadzic which he directly communicated to you and which you then communicated to the municipalities and attempted to implement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get some more specific details as regards which policy the Prosecutor is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness sought assistance on that question, but if he does we will address whatever inquiry he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I also need to know more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you in contact with Mr. Karadzic in 1991, telephone contact, personal contact?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, most probably I was. Now if you ask me 23 years later, I don't know whether it happened often. He had other commitments, not to speak to me on a daily basis. But if you are interested in which policy, I can only tell you exactly what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did he entrust to you the responsibility to ensure the implementation of positions that he had taken, the implementation of actions that he wanted to see taken on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there was no Mr. Karadzic policy, but rather the policy of the Serbian Democratic Party that won the elections at least in the Serbian entity and among the Serbian people. Secondly, perhaps -- but not perhaps, most probably, he charged me with this but I wasn't able to do it on my own. This was not the president's policy because that was the policy that had to be implemented at this particular point in time. Don't forget that we had lived in a beautiful country of Yugoslavia and the Serbs were the only people who were eager to preserve this country and prevent it from breaking up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two interventions in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 42 the witness said: Most probably I do not deny, is what he said. And just now he said that: He charged me with something but not with that. He used the word "something."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be much easier for everyone if the witness spoke more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you expressed your loyalty and commitment to the principle of hierarchy and the need to obey the commands of those above you and the need for those below you to obey the commands that you made or passed on; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: It's very difficult to give you a yes or no answer. Some people considered me as an opposition and other people considered me what you described as they saw fit. At any rate, at that point in time I was part of the winning team that won the elections, and of course I had my own opinions, but I did, however, often realise that I have to respect the opinion of the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, the nature of your relationship with Dr. Karadzic in 1991 was such that he, in one telephone conversation in late October of 1991, chided you for coming to him with every single little problem and told you that he's not your nanny, that you had the power in your hands and he wanted you to exercise that power energetically and fully. That's the truth of your relationship with Mr. Karadzic in 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: What follows from this is that we basically talked every day; however, you do have to know that Mr. Karadzic was so busy that if you'd call him twice in two months' time he could have said that and he usually would say that because he was way too busy. But please do not infer that we talked every day; I would not have had that opportunity. In 1991, conditionally speaking, I was unknown. It's not that I could talk to anybody whenever I wanted to. I mean, it's not that I was absolutely unknown. I don't want it to look as if I were lying now, but it's not that I was held in such regard that I could talk to whoever I wanted to whenever I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, in late October 1991, there was a meeting of all the municipality presidents and that happened in Banja Luka. And that resulted in the so-called Sarajevo -- the SDS order or Sarajevo order, which included such things as immediately forming commands of the town, setting up around-the-clock duty, full mobility of the Territorial Defence, taking over management in public enterprises, the post office, the SDK, and by all means the media, and other matters. And the person put in charge of implementing that was you; right? And that's a more accurate reflection of your relationship with the accused and your power at the time than what you told us in the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: In October 1991, I think as far as I can remember, I was vice-president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. I could receive such instructions within the autonomous region where there was a president and a president of the government, if you will, of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, and my answer would not really differ from my previous answer. All things that one had to do were not always based on trust. It depended on who had what kind of affinity for organisation. Perhaps it's because of my profession, because in the business sector I was always in charge of setting up some kind of organisation. That would imply good management or at least average of good management.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The document I referred to before is P3581, it's a 29 October 1991 Telex regarding the order of the SDS Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can call up 3581 and look to the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There you can see that you, sir, are the -- sending this out on behalf of Dr. Karadzic as the co-ordinator for implementing decisions, these decisions; right? So contrary to your previous emphasis on what you tried to characterise as your limited position, you are implementing these important -- you are charged with implementing these important decisions by Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Without wanting to pay you compliments, I believe that you're not in that position -- I mean, you are in that position because you're a good lawyer, and you know full well that co-ordinator does not mean that one has decision-making powers. And what it says here is "co-ordinator," and thank you for showing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I wasn't saying that you made that decision. I'm saying that you're in charge of co-ordinating the implementation of those decisions made at the republic level, and that's the truth of it, right? And that's a reflection of the power that was entrusted to you by Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat this once again. It is true that this came to me and that I was the co-ordinator, but if I may just say this regarding paragraphs 1 and 2, that was superfluous then and it is now. There was an army, the JNA then, that did not allow the establishment of any kind of town commands or whatever, and later on we are going to see when it was that the Army of Republika Srpska was established; however, what we inherited was the JNA because Yugoslavia was still in existence in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this Trial Chamber has received evidence that on September 7th, there was a meeting in Pale, the so-called Pale symposium, to make decisions regarding regionalisation and that on the 6th, Dr. Karadzic spoke to President Milosevic, told him he'd be holding this plenary with all his officials. That was held on the 7th and decisions were made, and we see an intercepted telephone conversation from a Main Board member describing the decision that was made about dividing Bosnia into units. Now, before that decision was made, before that meeting was held on the 7th of September, Dr. Karadzic called you and -- to advise you that there would be a meeting at which important things would be decided and that everything that you thought or wanted would happen but would move forward in a particular way, and that's reflected at P5886. And I want you to take a look at that quickly. Now, I want you to look at the second page of the English and the second page of the B/C/S as well. Okay. That's where Dr. Karadzic says: If you had brought the decision on the referendum, it would have been terrible. You tell him we have not -- have not obeyed. Dr. Karadzic tells you: There's no problem, Brdjo, come tomorrow, you will see --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we please see exactly where you're reading from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the English it's about the one-third down from the top of the page and in the B/C/S it's up at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You started reading from the line below the underlined sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you, Mr. President. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then we continue: "There is no problem, Brdjo, come tomorrow you will see. We do all and everything will be what you think, only, only way is ..." And then Dr. Karadzic goes on to describe what Tudjman is thinking, and then he talks about Van den Broek trying to convince Milosevic and he continues: "And now they need to mess that Conference up, and now they are looking for any way to mess that Conference up tomorrow ..." Now, that reference to the conference tomorrow is a reference to the opening of the Conference on Yugoslavia in the Peace Palace, right, on September 7th; correct? If you need some refreshment about the date, I have a document that would reflect that date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could we take a look at the date when this conversation took place so that we do not mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The date -- I'm suggesting that this intercept is misdated on its heading and I'm trying to contextualise it on the basis of exactly what was stated at the time with the witness, who was just about to confirm that it is a reference to the opening of the Conference on Yugoslavia because he was nodding his head "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Brdjanin, this is a reference to the Conference on Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do you recall on your own or would you like to see a document that indicates the conference opened on September 7th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't remember that it started on the 7th, but that's what you read out and I have no reason to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we can quickly turn to 65 ter 06436, and there we see the declaration on the occasion of the ceremonial opening of the Conference on Yugoslavia, Peace Palace, The Hague, 7 September 1991. I take it from your nodding your head that conforms to your general recollection of the date?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there's something important in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. If it's dealing with the subject we're dealing with.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: An intercept, when Mr. Karadzic says "you should," it doesn't pertain to me only but to the members of parliament. We had 17 presidents of municipalities, 20 MPs, Krajina was two-thirds of our entity. Here one gets the impression that it pertains to me only, no. It is all the representatives of the people from that part of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And with respect to your own authority, in contrast to other representatives of the Serbian people from that part of Republika Srpska, what your Trial Chamber found at paragraph 295 is that the top leadership of the Serbian BiH of Republika Srpska granted you a high degree of authority and autonomy in areas of fundamental political importance, which is indicative of the trust that you enjoyed at the highest political level. That's what your Trial Chamber concluded after the trial was completed about your own authority, in contrast to some of the other people you just referred to.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: It is correct that those were the findings of the Trial Chamber. That was the greatest surprise because the Trial Chamber found that I should be acquitted in terms of the joint criminal enterprise because their assessment was that often my views were quite different, not to say the opposite. But I do not see any document that shows that I was given some kind of political power. Which document is that? Minister of civil engineering, nowhere in the world is that political power. This is professional. Also the deputy prime minister in charge of economic affairs, I don't know, perhaps I don't understand this. But rest assured that my thoughts are sincere, that I'm not trying to hide anything, I'm just thinking out loud, and I have this opportunity now to say what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, we -- this Trial Chamber has heard evidence of the tensions surrounding the efforts to declare Krajina a republic, tensions that were resolved on the 29th of February, 1992, at the 14th Session of the ARK Assembly. And a couple of weeks after that Assembly, you explained to the public that while there were differences between the Banja Luka and Sarajevo options for solving the Serbian question, there were no divisions and that you people from Krajina did not wish to split-off from the body of the Serbian people in BH, but did want to split-off from Alija. And in that regard, let me assist you by showing you 65 ter 05419, a "Glas" newspaper article dated the 15th of March, 1992, which is D3070.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, that's -- that reflects your -- the newspaper article reflects your comments and positions in mid-March 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I see the comments and positions here, but may I respond to your question about us wanting to split-off from Alija?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't precisely the question I was really focused on, the division, but I see that the article raises your comment that you want to split-off from Alija. So if you have something to say briefly about that, please do so.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I made a mistake when I said that we wanted to split-off from Alija. Actually, it was Alija who wanted to split-off from Yugoslavia and from us, and we had no reason to split-off from anyone. Because at that point in time we were still defending Yugoslavia by all possible political means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Let me jump ahead now from mid-March, then, to the period shortly after the 16th Assembly Session which was held on May 12th, 1992, in Banja Luka. I mentioned that date in particular because you mentioned the -- yourself a few moments ago the establishment of the army and so on. So we can agree, I take it, that at the 16th Assembly Session in Banja Luka the VRS was formally established, General Mladic was selected as the commander of the Main Staff, the strategic objectives were annunciated by Dr. Karadzic, and there was a general discussion of the political and security situation at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, not more than three weeks after that session in Banja Luka, Dr. Karadzic met with you once again but this time in a somewhat smaller setting of more selected people, correct, also in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, do you have a document that could jog my memory? After all, it was 23 years ago, 22 years ago, I don't know exactly which meeting you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could we call up P1478, page 53 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, while we're waiting for the document to come up, this is an entry in the war journal kept by General Mladic between 1991 and 1995. And this reflects an entry for the 2nd of June, 1992, in Banja Luka, a meeting with the leaderships of the Bosnian Krajina, the SRK, and unit commanders of the 1st Krajina Corps, and the commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence of the Serbian BH. And if we -- I'll direct your attention to this in a moment, but if we -- well, let's -- familiarise yourself with what it says here. It's Dr. Karadzic who speaks about the issue of the functioning of authorities, talks about the tasks of the authorities, indicates that a decree has been issued on War Presidencies. Agents of the government will be sent to the junior organs of the authorities. If we can turn the page, there we see you speaking, and among the things you say is: "Everything in the ARK is done at Crisis Staff level because that is where the work -- that is where work all of. "It is a mistake to appoint agents from the centre ..." And if we can -- I --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV BRDJANIN
utterances.text: I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I mean, I can ask you about separate pieces of this, but I wanted to show you also before we -- before I ask you questions, another document which also reflects this meeting. So perhaps I can do that now. This is a document --
